TransPath-C identifies consistent pathway regulation across mouse and human platelet proteomes

TransPath-C identifies consistent pathway regulation across mouse and human platelet proteomes. (A) Schematic overview of the TransPath-C method. (B) Pathways with nonzero loadings in sPC2. Salmon indicates pathway enrichment in adult platelets. (C) Pathways with nonzero loadings in sPC3. Red indicates pathway enrichment in adult platelets. Blue indicates pathway enrichment in neonatal platelets. The x-axis is intentionally flipped to be directionally consistent with respect to neonatal or adult enrichment with panel B. (D) Krebs cycle comparison in human and mouse platelets. Red indicates higher protein abundance in neonatal platelets, and blue indicates higher protein abundance in adult platelets. (E) GPVI pathway comparison in human and mouse platelets. Red indicates higher protein abundance in neonatal platelets, and blue indicates higher protein abundance in adult platelets. Gray indicates proteins that were not detected in murine samples (LAT and DAG1). AD, adult; Neo, neonatal
